title: AI for All - Artificial Intelligence for Life, Society, and Disciplines

instructor.name: Dr. G. G. Md. Nawaz Ali
instructor.office_hours: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, 1:00 PM - 2:00 PM

description: A conceptual, applied course about artificial intelligence for students across disciplines. It emphasizes ethical reflection, entrepreneurial thinking, non-code AI and machine-learning tools, basic data wrangling, inference, visualization, responsible prompting, and critical evaluation of AI outputs for accuracy, bias, and limitations.
objectives: Understand foundational AI concepts and terminology.
Explain how AI systems function at a conceptual level.
Learn basics of data wrangling, interpretation, and visualization.
Use AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot effectively and responsibly.
Design and refine prompts for learning, writing, analysis, and decision support.
Critically evaluate AI outputs for bias, accuracy, and limitations.
Analyze ethical, social, and professional implications of AI technologies.
Connect AI concepts to disciplinary, ethical, and societal contexts.
learning_outcomes: Define AI in scientifically grounded terms and distinguish it from popular media portrayals.
Describe AI as an interdisciplinary field connecting computing, data, society, and ethics.
Apply AI for data interpretation and visualization.
Apply AI concepts to real-world problems relevant to an academic discipline.
Evaluate benefits, risks, and societal impacts of AI tools.
Demonstrate responsible and transparent AI usage practices.
Compare AI-assisted and non-AI approaches to problem solving.
Identify opportunities where AI can ethically create value within a discipline.
topics: Data wrangling and AI data pipelines
Generative AI and large language models
materials_and_tools: zyBook: Data Science & AI Literacy (Python Sandbox / Non-Code Focus)

title: Natural Language Processing & Large Language Models (NLP & LLMs)

instructor.name: Dr. G. G. Md. Nawaz Ali
instructor.office_hours: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, 1:00 PM - 2:00 PM

prerequisites: CS 461 or CS 462 or consent of instructor
description: An in-depth, hands-on study of natural language processing and large language models, progressing from foundational NLP to transformer-based models and production-style AI systems. The course emphasizes practical implementation, evaluation, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, tool-using LLMs, multi-agent systems, and neuro-symbolic reasoning.
objectives: Explain linguistic, statistical, and neural foundations of NLP.
Implement core NLP pipelines using Python and modern libraries.
Train, fine-tune, and evaluate transformer-based language models.
Apply pre-trained LLMs for downstream NLP tasks.
Design and implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems.
Integrate external tools and APIs with LLMs.
Analyze LLM limitations including hallucination, bias, and scalability.
Critically assess emerging trends in LLM research and deployment.
learning_outcomes: Construct NLP pipelines for text preprocessing, representation, and modeling.
Apply word, sentence, and document embeddings effectively.
Implement transformer architectures using existing deep learning frameworks.
Fine-tune large language models for task-specific applications.
Build end-to-end LLM systems incorporating retrieval, memory, and tools.
Evaluate NLP and LLM systems using appropriate quantitative metrics.
Communicate design decisions and trade-offs in advanced AI systems.
topics: Classical NLP: Bag-of-Words, TF-IDF, and N-grams
Sequence models: RNNs, LSTMs, and GRUs
Evaluation of NLP and LLM systems
materials_and_tools: Local GPU, Google Colab, Kaggle, or university computing resources
